title: C482/2289/2022 of MOHD YAKOOB Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY HOME, GOVERNMENT OF U.K. DEHRADUN

paras.text:
SL.
No Date
Office Notes, reports,
orders or proceedings
or directions and
Registrar's order with
Signatures
COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
14.02.2023 C482 No. 2289 of 2022
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Shariq Khurshid, Advocate, for
the applicants.
Mr. Pratiroop Pande, AGA, along
with Mr. Pramod Tiwari, Brief Holder, for
the State.
Mr. Sarfiroz, Advocate, holding brief
of Mr. Prince Chauhan, Advocate, for the
respondent.
The applicants are present in
person, who had been identified by the
respective learned counsel for the
applicants. Respondent No. 2, too is present
in person. She has been identified by the
learned counsel, representing her.
The proceedings which are subject
to challenge in the present C482
Application is emanating from a Criminal
Case No. 4031 of 2022, State Vs. Mohd.
Yakoob and others, where the summoning
order has been issued against the present
applicants for trying them for the offences
under Section 498A, 323, 504 & 506 of IPC
and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
It is an admitted case that out of the
matrimony, a girl child has born and
presently she is in the custody and care of
the complainant respondent No. 2.
Upon being interacted, the
complainant has submitted, that on account
of the atrocities exercised by the applicant

No. 2, and due to the humiliation, which was
faced by her while discharging her
matrimonial obligations, she submits that it
is practically impossible for her to endure
the atrocities for all times to come and
hence she has resolved to settle the dispute
as amongst themselves on the basis of the
settlement which has been arrived at
between the parties on 01.02.2023, which
has been placed on record by virtue of a
supplementary affidavit filed in support of
the Compounding Application.
The terms of settlement contained
in the supplementary affidavit would
constitute as to be the part of this order.
The parties, who are present in
person, have duly signed the Compounding
Application, the contents of which stand
verified by the respective counsels, who are
representing them. Since the dispute being
exclusively a private dispute and all the
offences would be compoundable under
Section 320 of CrPC, except for the offence
under Section 498A of IPC, which could be
compoundable with the leave of the Court
and particularly in order to resolve the
controversy and to put the parties at peace,
the Compounding Application is required to
be considered by this Court in the exercise
of its inherent jurisdiction under Section 482
of CrPC.
The factum of the execution of
settlement is a fact stated to be admitted by
all the parties. In that eventuality, this C482
Application would stand allowed and as a
consequence thereto, the proceedings of
Criminal Case No. 4031 of 2022, State Vs.

Mohd. Yakoob and others, pending
consideration before the Court of Additional
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kashipur, District
Udham Singh Nagar, would hereby stand
quashed in terms of the settlement, which
has been arrived at between the parties and
who are signatories to it that they would
religiously honour the terms of the
settlement in future.
Subject to aforesaid, the C482
Application stands closed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 14.02.2023
Mahinder/
